title: C137 — Windshield washer pump connector reference
introduction:
The washer pump moves fluid, but this page maps its electrical connection. I start with the connector identity table, then follow the cavity labels between the drawing and the pin assignments. Think of those labels as seat numbers: their printed identities matter more than which one appears first on the page.

That distinction is especially useful here because the drawing's vertical cavity order differs from the table's row order. Read the label before choosing the row, then follow that row across its circuit, wire, function and terminal fields. Housing Color in the identity table and wire Color in the pin table describe different things. The final table supplies the pigtail service cross-reference.

This reference explains identification and table reading. It supplies no physical viewing-side instruction, access method, probing setup, electrical acceptance values or replacement sequence. Leave Size and Used as recorded codes and retain Gauge entries without assuming a gauge convention.

edits.why: The rounded top, projecting feature on the left and stepped lower edge are useful landmarks within the supplied drawing. I read the cavity labels rather than assigning contacts by height. The Fpn and Harness Id beneath the illustration connect the picture to the connector record; the drawn layout alone does not establish the physical viewing side.

Cavity is the link back to the drawing. Function distinguishes the washer-control connection from the ground return, while Circuit Number names each circuit. Read wire Color, Gauge and Terminal Part Number across that same row. These assignments explain the recorded connections; they do not establish that the pump or either circuit is working.

The pigtail is the connector with attached wire leads. I use Kit List to find Number here and compare Engineering Shell with Hard Shell in the identity table. Service Part supplies the service reference, while Image names an illustration file. The material, gauge and cavity fields describe the listed pigtail; they do not supply a replacement or splice procedure.
